brief.title: Split the Codex runner into a service?
brief.question: Should BenchMemo extract repo probing into a separate service now, or keep the current in-process runner?

options.name: Keep the current in-process runner
options.description: Retain repo probing inside the current API process for now.

options.name: Extract a separate probe service
options.description: Move repo probing into a standalone service immediately.

frame.normalizedQuestion: Should BenchMemo extract repo probing into a separate service now, or keep the current in-process runner?

options.name: Keep the current in-process runner
options.description: Retain repo probing inside the current API process for now.

options.name: Extract a separate probe service
options.description: Move repo probing into a standalone service immediately.

criteria.name: Risk
criteria.scoringGuidance: Prefer the option with fewer hidden dependencies and less coordination risk.

criteria.name: Velocity
criteria.scoringGuidance: Prefer the option that keeps progress high in the current milestone.

claims.text: Keeping the runner in-process avoids hidden orchestration work.
claims.rationale: The current worker and API still share assumptions and tests.

opt_service.summary: A service split could create cleaner boundaries later.

claims.text: A separate service could isolate repo probing concerns.

opt_inline.summary: Inline execution can become crowded later.

claims.text: The current API process could become crowded over time.
claims.rationale: Future scale might still justify a split later.

opt_service.summary: The service split hides more coupling than it first appears.

claims.text: The probe worker is still tightly coupled to API orchestration and tests.
claims.rationale: A service split would spread one coherent path across more boundaries.

repoProbes.summary: Keeping the runner in-process preserves the current orchestration shape and keeps coupling explicit instead of distributing it across a network boundary.
A service split would require APIs, job handoff, and artifact contract changes while creating hidden coordination risk across orchestration, artifacts, and tests.
migrationHazards: Cross-process run coordination would be new.
More boundary contracts would need to stabilize at once.
operationalRisks: On-call diagnosis would span more moving parts.

evidenceItems.title: Current orchestration keeps probe coordination in one place
evidenceItems.excerpt: The current code already coordinates probe fan-out, artifacts, and final memo generation in one path.

evidenceItems.title: Service split would add hidden coupling across artifacts and run state
evidenceItems.excerpt: The current runner, artifacts, and schemas still move together, so an early split would create hidden coupling at the network boundary.

claimStatuses.notes: The current orchestration shape is coherent.
The proposed service split hides more coupling than it removes.
The inline path is not yet the pressing problem.
The coupling is real and near-term.

judgeDraft.executiveSummary: Keep the runner in-process for now because a service split would introduce hidden coupling across orchestration, artifacts, and tests before those contracts have stabilized.

criterionScores.rationale: Keeping the runner in-process avoids hidden coupling at a new network boundary.
The current path preserves focus during the milestone.
The service split creates hidden coupling across run state and artifacts.
Splitting now expands implementation surface during a short horizon.

keyRisks: A service split now would add coordination risk before the contracts are settled.
dissent: If the runner becomes a clear scaling bottleneck, a service split should be reconsidered later.
nextSteps: Map the shared contracts first if a future service split becomes necessary.
